title: H-0P3

contributors.contribution: Helped populate maps, items, stores, logistics, and other game content using a custom content-entry tool.

description: H-0P3 was an early mobile 4X-style space combat and trading game inspired by the classic BBS game Trade Wars. Built with JavaME and the BlackBerry SDK, it explored many of the systems I would later expand into larger space-game projects, including Bridge Captain.

sections.title: The Game
paragraphs: H-0P3 was a single-player 4X-style space combat and trading game built for early smartphones. It combined exploration, tactical combat, trading, resource gathering, ship management, and progression inside a larger galaxy structure.

sections.title: Game Systems
items: Real-time and automated tactical ship combat

sections.title: UI, Graphics & 3D
paragraphs: I designed and created the game's interface, graphics, ship presentation, 3D models, and other visual assets. H-0P3 was also my first mobile project to apply my own 3D mathematics to features such as the planetary scanning display.

sections.title: Mobile Combat & Controls
paragraphs: The interface and combat systems were designed around the constraints of early smartphones rather than desktop-style controls. Battles could progress automatically while the player made higher-level tactical decisions through compact on-screen controls and command updates.

sections.title: Content & Tooling
paragraphs: Two volunteer contributors helped populate H-0P3 with maps, items, stores, logistics, and other game content. I built a content-entry tool so they could contribute without editing source code or raw game data directly.

sections.title: Promotional Website
paragraphs: I also began building a promotional website for H-0P3 using the same visual language as the game. The site was not completed or used for a full marketing launch, but it included custom page layouts, navigation, ship and galaxy presentation, and original sci-fi UI and graphic design.

sections.title: Project Evolution
paragraphs: H-0P3 established a number of the space-game ideas I wanted to keep exploring. Rather than simply expanding the same release, I later moved those ideas into the much larger Bridge Captain project, where the scope grew into deeper exploration, narrative, ship systems, crew interaction, and tactical gameplay.

historicalNotes: H-0P3 was primarily an early mobile release used to gain experience with the BlackBerry/mobile ecosystem.
It was not expanded to Android or heavily marketed with trailers.
The original intention was to revisit and expand the concept, but Bridge Captain later became the larger successor direction.
Two volunteer content contributors helped populate maps, items, stores, logistics, and other game content using a custom tool Jamie built for them.
Jamie created the game's UI, graphics, 3D models, and other visual assets.
H-0P3 included Jamie's first mobile use of his own 3D mathematics for the planetary scanning presentation.
A promotional H-0P3 website was started but not completed or used for a full marketing launch.
Jamie created the promotional website's visual design, layouts, navigation, and graphics.
